title: Game of Thrones
note: Written by Claude for Watch Together. Moments are approximate (fraction of the runtime, in scene order). Production facts only - no spoilers beyond the episode.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Winter Is Coming (S1E1)

items.fact: The first pilot was largely reshot - several roles were recast, including Catelyn and Daenerys.
Winterfell's courtyard in Season 1 was filmed at Castle Ward in Northern Ireland.
The direwolf pups were played by Northern Inuit dogs in the early seasons; Sophie Turner later adopted the dog who played Lady.
'The things I do for love' - the ending shocked viewers who hadn't read George R. R. Martin's book.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Kingsroad (S1E2)

items.fact: Peter Dinklage was Benioff and Weiss's first and only choice for Tyrion.
Sophie Turner liked the dog who played Lady so much that her family adopted her after filming.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Lord Snow (S1E3)

items.fact: Castle Black and the base of the Wall were built in a disused quarry at Magheramorne, Northern Ireland.
Syrio Forel's 'water dancing' lessons were choreographed to look like Braavosi fencing - Miltos Yerolemou trained for weeks.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Cripples, Bastards, and Broken Things (S1E4)

items.fact: Tyrion designs a special saddle so Bran can ride again - a small kindness the show kept from the book.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Wolf and the Lion (S1E5)

items.fact: Several scenes between Robert and Cersei were written for the show - they have no direct counterpart in the book.
The street fight between Ned and Jaime was filmed in Malta, which stood in for King's Landing in Season 1.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – A Golden Crown (S1E6)

items.fact: Viserys's 'golden crown' was created with practical make-up and visual effects; Harry Lloyd played Viserys.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – You Win or You Die (S1E7)

items.fact: Critic Myles McNutt coined the word 'sexposition' about scenes like this one, where backstory is told during a brothel scene.
'When you play the game of thrones, you win or you die' - Cersei's line gave the episode its title.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Pointy End (S1E8)

items.fact: 'The first sword of Braavos does not run' - Syrio's last stand happens off-screen in the book as well.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Baelor (S1E9)

items.fact: The episode is named after the Great Sept of Baelor in King's Landing.
Killing the main star in episode 9 became the show's signature: the penultimate episode of each season is usually the biggest.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Fire and Blood (S1E10)

items.fact: The final image of Daenerys with three baby dragons was one of the most expensive VFX shots of Season 1.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The North Remembers (S2E1)

items.fact: From Season 2, King's Landing was filmed mainly in Dubrovnik, Croatia, instead of Malta.
Stephen Dillane joins as Stannis Baratheon, with Carice van Houten as Melisandre.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Night Lands (S2E2)

items.fact: The Iron Islands were filmed at Ballintoy harbour in Northern Ireland.

names: what is dead may never die
entries.title: Game of Thrones – What Is Dead May Never Die (S2E3)

items.fact: Gwendoline Christie trained for months for Brienne of Tarth - she gained muscle and cut her hair for the role.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Garden of Bones (S2E4)

items.fact: Qarth's exteriors were filmed in Croatia, around Dubrovnik and the island of Lokrum.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Ghost of Harrenhal (S2E5)

items.fact: Charles Dance's scenes with Maisie Williams at Harrenhal were invented for the show - in the book Arya serves Roose Bolton instead.

names: the old gods and the new
entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Old Gods and the New (S2E6)

items.fact: The snowy scenes beyond the Wall were filmed in Iceland from Season 2 onwards.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – A Man Without Honor (S2E7)

items.fact: Nikolaj Coster-Waldau's chained Jaime scenes were a showcase that convinced many viewers the character was more than a villain.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Prince of Winterfell (S2E8)

items.fact: This episode sets up 'Blackwater', the show's first full battle episode.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Blackwater (S2E9)

items.fact: 'Blackwater' was written by George R. R. Martin himself and directed by Neil Marshall (The Descent).
Bronn and the soldiers sing 'The Rains of Castamere'; the indie band The National recorded a version that plays over the end credits.
HBO gave the battle extra budget - it was the first episode the whole hour was set in one place.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Valar Morghulis (S2E10)

items.fact: 'Valar morghulis' - 'all men must die' in High Valyrian. The language was expanded for the show by linguist David J. Peterson.
The season ends on the first big reveal of the White Walkers' army, filmed in Iceland.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Valar Dohaeris (S3E1)

items.fact: 'Valar dohaeris' - 'all men must serve' - is the traditional reply to 'valar morghulis'.
Astapor's slave city was filmed in Essaouira, Morocco.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Dark Wings, Dark Words (S3E2)

items.fact: Diana Rigg (Emma Peel in 'The Avengers' TV series) joins as Olenna Tyrell, the Queen of Thorns.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Walk of Punishment (S3E3)

items.fact: The end credits play 'The Bear and the Maiden Fair' by the rock band The Hold Steady.

names: and now his watch is ended
entries.title: Game of Thrones – And Now His Watch Is Ended (S3E4)

items.fact: Emilia Clarke learned her High Valyrian speech phonetically; the reveal that Daenerys speaks it was kept from viewers until this moment.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Kissed by Fire (S3E5)

items.fact: Jaime's bath confession to Brienne is one of Nikolaj Coster-Waldau's most praised scenes.

names: the bear and the maiden fair
entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Bear and the Maiden Fair (S3E7)

items.fact: This episode was written by George R. R. Martin.
The bear was a real trained bear named Bart the Bear 2, filmed separately in the US and composited into the scene.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Rains of Castamere (S3E9)

items.fact: George R. R. Martin based this storyline on two real Scottish massacres: the Black Dinner (1440) and the Glencoe massacre (1692).
Benioff and Weiss said this was the scene that made them want to adapt the books in the first place.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Mhysa (S3E10)

items.fact: 'Mhysa' means 'mother' in Ghiscari; the closing crowd scene was filmed in Morocco with hundreds of extras.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Two Swords (S4E1)

items.fact: The wordless cold open shows Ned's sword Ice melted down into two new swords - set to 'The Rains of Castamere'.
Pedro Pascal joins as Oberyn Martell, years before The Mandalorian and The Last of Us.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Lion and the Rose (S4E2)

items.fact: This episode was written by George R. R. Martin.
The royal wedding set was one of the largest in the series; the 'Purple Wedding' nickname comes from the wine.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Breaker of Chains (S4E3)

items.fact: The siege of Meereen's exterior was filmed in Croatia (Klis Fortress) and Morocco.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Oathkeeper (S4E4)

items.fact: Jaime names the Valyrian steel sword he gives Brienne 'Oathkeeper'.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – First of His Name (S4E5)

items.fact: Dean-Charles Chapman took over Tommen in Season 4; he had earlier played a minor Lannister role.

names: the laws of gods and men
entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Laws of Gods and Men (S4E6)

items.fact: Peter Dinklage's trial speech ('I wish I was the monster you think I am') was filmed in a few takes and is a fan favourite.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Mountain and the Viper (S4E8)

items.fact: Hafþór Júlíus Björnsson, who plays the Mountain, later won the World's Strongest Man title (2018).

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Watchers on the Wall (S4E9)

items.fact: Neil Marshall, who directed 'Blackwater', returned for this full-episode battle at Castle Black.
The giant scythe on the Wall was the show's own addition - it isn't in the book.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Wars to Come (S5E1)

items.fact: This is the series' first flashback - young Cersei meets the witch Maggy.

names: the house of black and white
entries.title: Game of Thrones – The House of Black and White (S5E2)

items.fact: The Titan of Braavos was created with VFX; the Braavos streets were filmed in Šibenik, Croatia.
Dorne's Water Gardens were filmed at the Alcázar of Seville in Spain.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – High Sparrow (S5E3)

items.fact: Jonathan Pryce (Brazil, Evita) joins as the High Sparrow.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Sons of the Harpy (S5E4)

items.fact: The Sand Snakes are introduced in Dorne; their scenes were filmed in Spain.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Unbowed, Unbent, Unbroken (S5E6)

items.fact: 'Unbowed, Unbent, Unbroken' are the words of House Martell.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Gift (S5E7)

items.fact: The first meeting of Tyrion and Daenerys - fans had waited five seasons; it hasn't happened yet in the books.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Hardhome (S5E8)

items.fact: Directed by Miguel Sapochnik, whose work here led to him directing 'Battle of the Bastards' and 'The Long Night'.
The Hardhome battle was filmed over several weeks in a quarry in Northern Ireland.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Dance of Dragons (S5E9)

items.fact: The fighting pit scenes were filmed at the Plaza de toros in Osuna, Spain.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Mother's Mercy (S5E10)

items.fact: Lena Headey's walk of atonement used a body double, Rebecca Van Cleave, for the full-body shots; filmed in Dubrovnik.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Red Woman (S6E1)

items.fact: Carice van Houten's final reveal used prosthetics and VFX; Season 6 was the first to go beyond the published books.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Home (S6E2)

items.fact: Sebastian Croft plays young Ned Stark in Bran's visions; Max von Sydow plays the Three-Eyed Raven.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Oathbreaker (S6E3)

items.fact: The Tower of Joy fight was filmed in Spain; young Ned is played by Robert Aramayo.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Book of the Stranger (S6E4)

items.fact: The reunion at Castle Black is the first time two Stark children meet on screen since Season 1.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Door (S6E5)

items.fact: 'Hold the door' - George R. R. Martin told the showrunners Hodor's origin years earlier; Kristian Nairn played Hodor.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Broken Man (S6E7)

items.fact: Ian McShane plays Septon Ray in this episode - the first cold open before the opening credits in the series.
Bella Ramsey's Lyanna Mormont became a fan favourite after this one scene; Ramsey later starred in The Last of Us.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – No One (S6E8)

items.fact: The chase through Braavos was filmed in Girona, Spain.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Battle of the Bastards (S6E9)

items.fact: Miguel Sapochnik directed; the battle took 25 days to film with around 500 extras and 70 horses.
The famous 'pile of bodies' shots mixed stunt performers, dummies and digital doubles.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Winds of Winter (S6E10)

items.fact: The opening is scored by Ramin Djawadi's 'Light of the Seven' - the first time the show used a piano.
The episode is named after Martin's long-awaited sixth book, still unpublished when it aired.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Dragonstone (S7E1)

items.fact: The singing Lannister soldier is Ed Sheeran - a cameo arranged because Maisie Williams is a fan.
Dragonstone's exteriors were filmed at Gaztelugatxe and Zumaia in Spain's Basque Country.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Queen's Justice (S7E3)

items.fact: Kit Harington and Emilia Clarke's first scene together - fans had waited seven seasons.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Spoils of War (S7E4)

items.fact: The loot train battle was filmed in Spain and is one of the few times the show put its dragon against a full army in daylight.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Eastwatch (S7E5)

items.fact: Joe Dempsie returns as Gendry, who had been 'rowing' since Season 3 - a running fan joke.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Beyond the Wall (S7E6)

items.fact: The frozen lake island was filmed in Iceland and on a huge Belfast stage.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Dragon and the Wolf (S7E7)

items.fact: At about 80 minutes, this was the longest episode of the series up to that point.
The Dragonpit was filmed at the Roman amphitheatre ruins of Itálica near Seville, Spain.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – Winterfell (S8E1)

items.fact: The final season got a reworked opening title sequence that shows the Wall breached.

names: a knight of the seven kingdoms
entries.title: Game of Thrones – A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms (S8E2)

items.fact: Podrick's song 'Jenny of Oldstones' was set to music for the show; Florence + the Machine recorded it for the end credits.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Long Night (S8E3)

items.fact: The battle of Winterfell took 55 consecutive night shoots to film, directed by Miguel Sapochnik.
Many viewers complained the episode was too dark to see - the cinematographer said it was meant to be watched in a dark room.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Last of the Starks (S8E4)

items.fact: A disposable coffee cup left on the table during the feast made headlines; HBO digitally removed it days after airing.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Bells (S8E5)

items.fact: The destruction of King's Landing was filmed on a large backlot set in Northern Ireland plus Dubrovnik.

entries.title: Game of Thrones – The Iron Throne (S8E6)

items.fact: The series finale was written and directed by David Benioff and D. B. Weiss.
The Iron Throne prop is said to be made of swords - the show's version is far smaller than the one described in the books.
